text: "All Scripture is given by inspiration of God" is one Greek word: God-breathed. The breath that made Adam a living being is in your Bible.
explanation:
Theopneustos: God-breathed. In Genesis, God breathed into Adam's nostrils and he became a living soul. Every time you open the Word, God is breathing on you again. That's why Proverbs says His words "are life to those who find them, and health to all their flesh."

The word for "all" is kol: every part. Medicines target one area and often bring side effects elsewhere. God's Word brings health to all your flesh, from the crown of your head to the soles of your feet, with no side effects.

text: Jesus proved the resurrection from one word: God said "I am" the God of Abraham, not "I was."
explanation:
The Sadducees, who denied the resurrection, tried to trap Jesus with a riddle. He answered, "Have you not read what was spoken to you by God, saying, 'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living." Abraham had died centuries earlier, yet God said "I am" his God. He's alive.

Paul built an argument on a single letter: "He does not say, 'And to seeds,' as of many, but as of one, 'And to your Seed,' who is Christ." Every word of Scripture is inspired, down to the smallest letter. You can lean your whole weight on it.

text: A sleepless night plus reading the Book equals a turnaround. Ask the king of Persia.
explanation:
Haman's plot to destroy the Jews was moving fast. Then "that night the king could not sleep," so he had the book of the chronicles read to him. He heard how Mordecai had once exposed an assassination plot, and learned he'd never been rewarded. By morning, Haman was leading Mordecai through the streets in royal robes, and the whole story turned.

When you can't sleep, whether in a literal night or a night season, open the Book. God's records are full of what He has done. Read them, and give Jesus the honour He deserves. Your turnaround may hinge on that one sleepless night.

text: Three thousand years before germs were discovered, Moses wrote, "The life of the flesh is in the blood."
explanation:
For centuries doctors practised bloodletting, draining blood to drain disease; George Washington died after it, with a Bible near his bed that said life is in the blood. The Law required washing after touching the dead and isolating contagious skin disease, long before anyone knew about microbes. When a Jewish doctor in 1840s Vienna made doctors wash their hands, deaths on his ward plunged.

The oldest book in the Bible says God "hangs the earth on nothing," while ancient peoples imagined it resting on turtles or giants. Isaiah speaks of "the circle of the earth." Scripture isn't a science textbook, but when it touches science, it's accurate.

text: "Do not fear, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them."
explanation:
Elisha's servant woke to find their city surrounded by a Syrian army: horses, chariots, soldiers everywhere. He panicked. Elisha prayed, "Lord, open his eyes," and suddenly he saw the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire all around them.

What you see isn't all there is. There are more angels with you than there are demons against you. "Greater is He who is in you than he who is in the world." Don't become so focused on what the enemy is doing that you forget who's standing guard around you.

text: "When one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away." The mirror in which you behold His glory is the Word.
explanation:
Paul says that when Moses is read, a veil lies over many hearts. They see the letter but miss the revelation. "Nevertheless when one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away." Then: "We all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image."

You don't transform yourself by willpower. You behold Him, and the Spirit changes you into His image. So before you read, turn to Jesus: "Lord, open my eyes to see You." Keep a pen nearby. Become hungry for fresh revelation, because yesterday's manna won't feed you today.

text: "Have you not read?" Jesus asked again and again. Many of our problems come from not reading.
explanation:
"You are mistaken, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God." When tempted in the wilderness, the Son of God didn't rely on a feeling or a new word. He said, "It is written," three times.

The one who delights in God's Word and meditates on it day and night "shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water… whose leaf also shall not wither; and whatever he does shall prosper." Have your own Bible. Read it slowly, write in the margins, and let God speak to you through it.
